target.name: Atomic Industries
target.founder: Aaron Slodov, Austin Bishop, Lou Young Jr

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $25M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
Atomic Industries is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by Aaron Slodov, Austin Bishop, and Lou Young Jr., having raised $25M+ to date. The valuation analysis incorporates a comparable universe of nine robotics and manufacturing firms—one public and eight private—including recent-stage peers such as Generalist AI ($2.0B Series B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B Series B), and Walden Robotics ($1.1B Seed).

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, grounding on the $25M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a typical 2.0x step-up multiplier from Series A forward, implies a valuation of $50M. Peer-median analysis across four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables yields a median valuation of $1.7B, with a range from $1.1B to $2.0B. The wide dispersion reflects stage heterogeneity in the peer set, with three comps at Series B and one at Seed.

The triangulated analysis supports a broad range of $42M (low) to $2.0B (high), with a median estimate of $875M. The substantial gap between stage-progression and peer methods reflects tension between Atomic's earlier stage positioning and the elevated valuations recently commanded by robotics peers. Key uncertainties include the company's current revenue trajectory, competitive positioning within the peer set, and whether comparable valuations will sustain in the current environment.
